    People also ask
    Is Gonzaga a Mormon school?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    No,
    Gonzaga University is not a Mormon (LDS) school. It is a private, Roman Catholic, and Jesuit institution located in Spokane, Washington. Founded in 1887, the university is rooted in Jesuit values, which emphasize educating the whole person—mind, body, and spirit—while welcoming students from all religious backgrounds. 
    • Catholic/Jesuit Identity: Gonzaga's history is deeply intertwined with the Jesuit order, focusing on intellectual competence, community service, and social justice.
    • Diverse Community: While Catholic, the university is not restricted to Catholic students and includes individuals from diverse religious traditions.
    • Religious Life: The University Ministry team notes that while they are a Catholic university, they welcome all, including students from other faiths (e.g., Mormon students) who choose to study there
      .
       
    Therefore, Gonzaga is distinct from schools affiliated with The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (such as BYU).

      Description

      Gonzaga College High School is a private Catholic college-preparatory high school for boys in Washington, D.C. Founded by the Jesuits in 1821 as the Washington Seminary, Gonzaga is named in honor of Aloysius Gonzaga, an Italian saint from the 16th century. Gonzaga is the oldest boys' high school in Washington, D.C. Wikipedia
